Famous plays, by first performance.Lysistrata: Aristophanes' comedy has the women of Greece refuse sex until the men end the Peloponnesian War, and it is still staged around the world.
Famous plays, by first performance.Hamlet: Hamlet is Shakespeare's longest play at over 4,000 lines, and the Prince of Denmark has more lines than any other Shakespearean character.
Famous plays, by first performance.Tartuffe: Molière's comedy about a pious fraud so offended church circles that public performances were banned for years despite Louis XIV's support.
Famous plays, by first performance.A Doll's House: Ibsen's play ends with Nora slamming the door on her marriage, a scandal so intense that a German production got an alternative ending.
Famous plays, by first performance.Importance of Being Earnest: Wilde called it a trivial comedy for serious people; it opened weeks before the libel case and arrest that ended his career.
Famous plays, by first performance.The Cherry Orchard: Chekhov insisted his last play was a comedy, though Stanislavski staged it as a tragedy. He died only months after its premiere.
Famous plays, by first performance.A Streetcar Named Desire: Tennessee Williams' drama made Marlon Brando a star as Stanley Kowalski and won the Pulitzer Prize for Drama.
Famous plays, by first performance.Death of a Salesman: Arthur Miller's tragedy of Willy Loman won the Pulitzer Prize and a Tony, and made the line "attention must be paid" famous.
Famous plays, by first performance.The Mousetrap: Agatha Christie's whodunit has run in London since 1952, the longest continuous run in the world. Audiences are asked not to reveal the ending.
Famous plays, by first performance.Waiting for Godot: Beckett's tragicomedy has two men wait beside a tree for someone who never arrives. Asked who Godot was, Beckett said he would have said so in the play.

Baking a loaf of bread, in order.Measure the flour: Bakers weigh flour rather than scoop it, because a scooped cup can vary by 20 percent or more.
Baking a loaf of bread, in order.Mix the dough: Once wet, two flour proteins link up into gluten, which gives bread its stretchy structure.
Baking a loaf of bread, in order.Knead: Kneading lines up the gluten into sheets, and bakers test it by stretching a piece thin enough to see light through.
Baking a loaf of bread, in order.First rise: Yeast eats the sugars in flour and releases carbon dioxide, and the trapped gas makes the dough grow.
Baking a loaf of bread, in order.Punch down: This redistributes the yeast and pops big bubbles, giving a finer, more even crumb.
Baking a loaf of bread, in order.Shape the loaf: Shaping builds surface tension so the loaf holds its form and rises up rather than spreading out.
Baking a loaf of bread, in order.Second rise (proof): 'Proof' comes from an older meaning, to test: bakers originally proved that their yeast was alive.
Baking a loaf of bread, in order.Score the top: The slashes tell the loaf where to expand during oven spring, so it doesn't burst open in random spots.
Baking a loaf of bread, in order.Bake: Steam in the oven's first minutes keeps the crust flexible so it can expand, and the Maillard reaction browns it.
Baking a loaf of bread, in order.Cool on a rack: Bread keeps cooking as it cools and steam escapes, so slicing too soon can leave the crumb gummy.

Viking Age events, in order.Raid on Lindisfarne: The raid on this island monastery off northern England horrified Europe and is traditionally taken as the start of the Viking Age.
Viking Age events, in order.Vikings found Dublin: The Norse built a ship base here on the River Liffey; the name comes from Irish Dubh Linn, the black pool, and Dublin stayed Norse-ruled for centuries.
Viking Age events, in order.Great Heathen Army lands: This Danish force conquered East Anglia, Northumbria and Mercia, leaving Alfred's Wessex as the last English kingdom standing.
Viking Age events, in order.Iceland first settled: Tradition says Ingólfr Arnarson threw his high-seat pillars overboard to find where to settle, and they washed up at what became Reykjavik.
Viking Age events, in order.Rollo granted Normandy: The Frankish king gave the Viking leader land around the Seine; the region became Normandy, and his descendant William later conquered England.
Viking Age events, in order.Iceland's Althing founded: Held at Þingvellir, the Althing is often called the world's oldest surviving parliament, where chieftains settled laws and disputes.
Viking Age events, in order.Erik the Red settles Greenland: Exiled from Iceland for killings, he explored a new land and gave it a pleasant name, Greenland, to lure settlers.
Viking Age events, in order.Leif Erikson reaches Vinland: Roughly 500 years before Columbus, the Norse reached North America; L'Anse aux Meadows in Newfoundland is the proven site.
Viking Age events, in order.Cnut becomes King of England: He ruled England, Denmark and Norway as a North Sea empire, and legend says he once proved to flatterers that he could not command the tide.
Viking Age events, in order.Battle of Stamford Bridge: Harold Godwinson beat the Norwegian king Harald Hardrada here, then marched south and lost to William at Hastings a few weeks later.

Pregnancy milestones, by week.Embryo implants: About a week after conception the ball of cells burrows into the lining of the uterus, and the pregnancy truly begins.
Pregnancy milestones, by week.Positive pregnancy test: Tests detect hCG, a hormone made by the placenta-to-be, whose level roughly doubles every couple of days in early pregnancy.
Pregnancy milestones, by week.Heartbeat seen on ultrasound: At this stage the tiny heart is a flicker, beating around 100 times a minute and speeding up quickly to over 150.
Pregnancy milestones, by week.Embryo becomes a fetus: The shift in name marks that every major organ has begun to form, and the fetus is now roughly the size of a kumquat.
Pregnancy milestones, by week.First trimester ends: Many people wait until now to announce, since the risk of miscarriage drops sharply after this milestone.
Pregnancy milestones, by week.First kicks felt: The first flutter, called quickening, is often mistaken for gas, and second-time parents tend to feel it earlier.
Pregnancy milestones, by week.Age of viability: Babies born around now can survive with intensive care, though the risk of complications is still high.
Pregnancy milestones, by week.Third trimester begins: The baby puts on much of its birth weight in these final months, and its brain growth speeds up.
Pregnancy milestones, by week.Full term: Only about 5 percent of babies arrive on their actual due date, so most births land a bit earlier or later.
Pregnancy milestones, by week.Officially post-term: Past this point doctors usually recommend inducing labor, because the placenta may become less efficient.

Scientific laws, by when they were state.Kepler's third law: It links a planet's orbital period to its distance from the Sun, a pattern that later helped Newton uncover gravity.
Scientific laws, by when they were state.Boyle's law: The pressure of a gas rises as its volume shrinks, which is why scuba divers must exhale on the way up.
Scientific laws, by when they were state.Hooke's law: The force of a spring is proportional to its stretch; Hooke first published it as a coded anagram to protect his claim.
Scientific laws, by when they were state.Coulomb's law: Using a delicate torsion balance, he showed that electric force falls off with the square of distance, just as gravity does.
Scientific laws, by when they were state.Avogadro's law: Equal volumes of gas hold equal numbers of molecules; the idea was ignored for decades, and Avogadro's number came later.
Scientific laws, by when they were state.Ohm's law: Georg Ohm's finding that voltage equals current times resistance was initially mocked by his critics.
Scientific laws, by when they were state.Faraday's law of induction: A changing magnetic field creates a current, the principle behind power plants and transformers.
Scientific laws, by when they were state.Doppler effect: The pitch of a passing siren rises and falls because of it, and the same effect shifts the color of distant galaxies.
Scientific laws, by when they were state.Planck's law: His attempt to explain glowing hot objects introduced quanta of energy, the beginning of quantum theory.
Scientific laws, by when they were state.Hubble's law: Galaxies recede at speeds proportional to their distance, showing that the universe is expanding.

Areas of simple shapes.Equilateral triangle, side 1: Triangles are rigid, which is why bridges and roof trusses use them.
Areas of simple shapes.Right triangle, legs 1 and 1: It is exactly half of a unit square, split along the diagonal.
Areas of simple shapes.Circle, diameter 1: Of all shapes with the same perimeter, the circle encloses the most area.
Areas of simple shapes.Square, side 1: Squaring a number gets its name from this shape, because the area of a square with side n is n squared.
Areas of simple shapes.Regular pentagon, side 1: Its area involves the golden ratio, which is also the ratio of its diagonal to its side.
Areas of simple shapes.Regular hexagon, side 1: Bees use it because it tiles perfectly with the least wall material.
Areas of simple shapes.Circle, radius 1: It is pi itself, the number Archimedes trapped between polygons and the namesake of Pi Day, March 14.
Areas of simple shapes.Square, side 2: Doubling a side quadruples the area, a scaling rule that holds for every flat shape.
Areas of simple shapes.Regular octagon, side 1: The shape of stop signs; its area equals 2 plus 2 times the square root of 2, per unit side squared.
Areas of simple shapes.Cube surface, edge 1: For a given volume, a cube has the least surface among boxes, and six faces here give 6 square units.

When these big scientific ideas were put.Sun-centered solar system: Copernicus published it as he lay dying, and it placed the Sun at the center.
When these big scientific ideas were put.Laws of planetary motion: Kepler showed planets move in ellipses, not circles, as part of his work in Astronomia Nova.
When these big scientific ideas were put.Universal gravitation: Newton's Principia explained everything from falling apples to planetary orbits with one law.
When these big scientific ideas were put.Natural selection: Darwin's book appeared after Wallace had independently reached the same idea.
When these big scientific ideas were put.Mendel's laws of inheritance: Gregor Mendel, an Augustinian friar, bred peas, and his work was ignored until 1900.
When these big scientific ideas were put.Periodic table: Mendeleev left gaps for elements not yet discovered and correctly predicted several, such as gallium.
When these big scientific ideas were put.Special relativity: Einstein produced this as a 26-year-old patent clerk in his miracle year.
When these big scientific ideas were put.Continental drift: Alfred Wegener's idea was dismissed until plate tectonics vindicated it in the 1960s.
When these big scientific ideas were put.Uncertainty principle: Heisenberg found that you cannot know a particle's position and momentum both precisely.
When these big scientific ideas were put.DNA double helix: Watson and Crick's paper ran barely over a page and used Rosalind Franklin's data.

When space rocks slammed into Earth.Vredefort, South Africa: Vredefort is the largest verified impact structure on Earth, once about 300 km wide, and is now a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
When space rocks slammed into Earth.Sudbury, Canada: The impact left a basin rich in nickel and copper, which is why the city of Sudbury grew into one of the world's great mining centers.
When space rocks slammed into Earth.Acraman, Australia: Now largely eroded, this crater lies beneath a salt lake in the Gawler Ranges, but its debris has been found in rocks hundreds of kilometers away.
When space rocks slammed into Earth.Manicouagan, Canada: Its ring-shaped lake, nicknamed the Eye of Quebec, is so large and round that astronauts easily spot it from orbit.
When space rocks slammed into Earth.Chicxulub (dinosaur killer): The crater off Mexico's Yucatan, about 180 km wide, is tied to the extinction of the non-avian dinosaurs and a worldwide layer of iridium.
When space rocks slammed into Earth.Chesapeake Bay crater: Buried under the bay, this roughly 85 km crater probably shaped the Chesapeake's odd outline and left salty groundwater beneath nearby land.
When space rocks slammed into Earth.Ries crater, Germany: The town of Nordlingen sits inside it, and its church is built from impact rock; Apollo astronauts trained here to study such craters.
When space rocks slammed into Earth.Meteor Crater, Arizona: Also called Barringer Crater, it is about 1.2 km wide and was the first crater ever proven to come from a meteorite impact.
When space rocks slammed into Earth.Tunguska blast: This Siberian airburst flattened roughly 2,000 square kilometers of forest, yet left no crater because the object exploded in the air.
When space rocks slammed into Earth.Carancas, Peru: A small meteorite landed near Lake Titicaca and dug a crater about 13 m wide; nearby villagers reported sickness from the fumes.

Forgotten 19th-century US presidents, in.James K. Polk: He expanded the US to the Pacific, acquiring Oregon and California, and served just one term, as he had promised.
Forgotten 19th-century US presidents, in.Zachary Taylor: A career soldier, he had never voted in an election before he was elected president, and he died in office after about 16 months.
Forgotten 19th-century US presidents, in.Millard Fillmore: The last Whig president, he and his wife founded the White House's first library.
Forgotten 19th-century US presidents, in.Franklin Pierce: He affirmed rather than swore the oath of office, after losing his son in a train crash just before inauguration.
Forgotten 19th-century US presidents, in.James Buchanan: The only president who never married, he led the country just before the Civil War.
Forgotten 19th-century US presidents, in.Andrew Johnson: The first president to be impeached, he survived the Senate trial by a single vote, and he had been a tailor.
Forgotten 19th-century US presidents, in.Rutherford B. Hayes: He won the 1876 election by a single electoral vote, and during his term the White House got its first telephone.
Forgotten 19th-century US presidents, in.James A. Garfield: Shot in 1881, he lingered for about two months, and Alexander Graham Bell tried a metal detector to find the bullet.
Forgotten 19th-century US presidents, in.Chester A. Arthur: Succeeded after Garfield's death, he signed the Pendleton Act, which began a merit-based civil service.
Forgotten 19th-century US presidents, in.Benjamin Harrison: Grandson of an earlier president, he lost the popular vote in 1888 but won the electoral college.

Lesser-known programming languages by de.Lisp: Created by John McCarthy, it is the second-oldest high-level language still in use, after Fortran, and writes code as nested lists.
Lesser-known programming languages by de.Simula: Developed in Norway, it introduced classes and objects, ideas that later shaped C++ and Java.
Lesser-known programming languages by de.Pascal: Niklaus Wirth named it after mathematician Blaise Pascal, and it was taught to beginners for decades.
Lesser-known programming languages by de.SQL: Created at IBM as SEQUEL and renamed over a trademark issue, it still dominates database queries.
Lesser-known programming languages by de.Erlang: Built by Ericsson for telephone switches, it prized reliability, and WhatsApp's servers ran on it.
Lesser-known programming languages by de.Haskell: Named after logician Haskell Curry, it is a purely functional language that has influenced many modern ones.
Lesser-known programming languages by de.Lua: Created in Brazil, its name is Portuguese for moon, and it is embedded in games such as Roblox.
Lesser-known programming languages by de.Ruby: Yukihiro Matsumoto designed it for programmer happiness, and it powers the Rails web framework.
Lesser-known programming languages by de.Scala: Its name comes from scalable, and it blends object-oriented and functional styles on the Java virtual machine.
Lesser-known programming languages by de.Rust: It grew from a Mozilla employee's side project and has topped Stack Overflow's most-loved language surveys for years.

Milestones in artificial intelligence.Turing's imitation game paper: Alan Turing's 1950 paper asked 'Can machines think?' and proposed that a machine that fools a judge in text chat could count as thinking.
Milestones in artificial intelligence.Dartmouth AI workshop: John McCarthy coined 'artificial intelligence' for this summer gathering in New Hampshire, which is commonly seen as the birth of the field.
Milestones in artificial intelligence.Perceptron: Frank Rosenblatt's early neural network learned to recognize simple patterns, and a 1969 critique later froze much of the research for years.
Milestones in artificial intelligence.ELIZA chatbot: Joseph Weizenbaum's MIT program imitated a therapist by rephrasing statements as questions, and many users were convinced that it understood them.
Milestones in artificial intelligence.Lighthill report: This British government assessment criticized AI progress, and led to deep funding cuts, starting an 'AI winter' in the field.
Milestones in artificial intelligence.AlexNet: This image-recognition network won the ImageNet contest by a big margin, using graphics chips, and it set off the deep learning boom.
Milestones in artificial intelligence.GANs invented: Ian Goodfellow and colleagues pitted two neural networks against each other, one forging images and one detecting the fakes.
Milestones in artificial intelligence.Transformer paper: Google researchers' 'Attention Is All You Need' introduced the architecture underlying modern chatbots like ChatGPT.
Milestones in artificial intelligence.GPT-3: OpenAI's language model had 175 billion parameters, and it showed it could handle new tasks from just a few examples in its prompt.
Milestones in artificial intelligence.Stable Diffusion: This open image-generating model could run on a home graphics card, which let the public create pictures from text prompts.

Best Animated Feature Oscar winners.Shrek: DreamWorks' ogre comedy took the first-ever Best Animated Feature award, and its swamp-dwelling hero is a parody of fairy tales.
Best Animated Feature Oscar winners.Spirited Away: Hayao Miyazaki's bathhouse-of-spirits fantasy won, and he skipped the ceremony, reportedly protesting the Iraq war.
Best Animated Feature Oscar winners.Happy Feet: The tap-dancing penguin film from George Miller, who also made Mad Max, won in 2007, and its dance moves were captured from tap dancer Savion Glover.
Best Animated Feature Oscar winners.Rango: The chameleon western, voiced by Johnny Depp, was the first Oscar-winning film for Industrial Light and Magic's animation division.
Best Animated Feature Oscar winners.Frozen: The Disney film's 'Let It Go' also won Best Original Song, and the film grossed over a billion dollars at the box office.
Best Animated Feature Oscar winners.Big Hero 6: This Disney tale of a boy and his inflatable healthcare robot, Baymax, was inspired by an obscure Marvel comic, and it is set in a mashup city, San Fransokyo.
Best Animated Feature Oscar winners.Into the Spider-Verse: This film used comic-book textures and a Brooklyn teen hero, and it ended a seven-year run of wins by Disney and Pixar.
Best Animated Feature Oscar winners.Encanto: Disney's story of the magical Madrigal family, with its song 'We Don't Talk About Bruno', became a global streaming phenomenon.
Best Animated Feature Oscar winners.Guillermo del Toro's Pinocchio: The stop-motion version, by the Mexican director, set the story in fascist Italy, and it took years to make with puppets.
Best Animated Feature Oscar winners.Flow: Latvia's dialogue-free film about a cat after a flood made by Gints Zilbalodis was the first Latvian film to win an Oscar.

When these Egyptian monuments were built.Step Pyramid of Djoser: Djoser's Step Pyramid, designed by the architect Imhotep, was the first large stone building and the world's first pyramid.
When these Egyptian monuments were built.Great Pyramid of Giza: The Great Pyramid of Giza was the tallest human-made structure for around 3,800 years, and it is the only surviving ancient wonder.
When these Egyptian monuments were built.Karnak temple begun: Karnak is not a single temple but a complex built and added to by many pharaohs over about 2,000 years.
When these Egyptian monuments were built.Valley of the Kings first used: The Valley of the Kings, near Luxor, holds tombs of pharaohs like Tutankhamun, who was buried here instead of in a pyramid.
When these Egyptian monuments were built.Luxor Temple: Luxor Temple was connected to Karnak by an avenue lined with sphinxes, which was used for an annual festival.
When these Egyptian monuments were built.Abu Simbel: Abu Simbel's temples, carved into a cliff by Ramesses II, were cut into pieces and moved in the 1960s to save them from rising water behind Aswan Dam.
When these Egyptian monuments were built.Medinet Habu: Medinet Habu is the mortuary temple of Ramesses III, and its walls record the battles with the Sea Peoples.
When these Egyptian monuments were built.Lighthouse of Alexandria: The Lighthouse of Alexandria, one of the Seven Wonders, stood over 100 meters tall and guided ships until earthquakes destroyed it.
When these Egyptian monuments were built.Temple of Edfu begun: The Temple of Edfu, dedicated to the falcon god Horus, is among the best-preserved ancient temples, and took around 180 years to build.
When these Egyptian monuments were built.Dendera temple: Dendera's temple of Hathor features a famous ceiling with the zodiac, which was taken to Paris and now hangs in the Louvre.

Ancient Olympic events, by debut.Stadion (sprint): One lap of the stadium, about 192 metres, was the only event at the first 13 Games, and its winner gave his name to that Olympiad.
Ancient Olympic events, by debut.Diaulos (two lengths): Two lengths of the track, roughly 400 metres, added in 724 BC; runners had to turn around a post at the far end and sprint back.
Ancient Olympic events, by debut.Dolichos (long race): The long race ran somewhere between 7 and 24 laps, and ancient sources disagree on its exact length, so nobody knows the true distance.
Ancient Olympic events, by debut.Pentathlon: Five events: sprint, long jump, discus, javelin and wrestling. Jumpers swung stone or lead weights called halteres to carry them further.
Ancient Olympic events, by debut.Boxing: Fighters wrapped their hands in leather straps, and there were no rounds or weight classes, so a bout went on until one man gave up.
Ancient Olympic events, by debut.Four-horse chariot race: The prize went to the owner, not the driver, so wealthy women and even kings could be Olympic champions by simply entering a team.
Ancient Olympic events, by debut.Pankration: A brutal blend of boxing and wrestling in which only biting and eye-gouging were banned; some fighters died in the contest.
Ancient Olympic events, by debut.Boys' sprint: The first age-group event: boys raced for the same wild-olive wreath, cut from a sacred tree at Olympia, that the men won.
Ancient Olympic events, by debut.Race in armour: Runners carried a heavy shield and wore a helmet in this test of soldier fitness, often staged as the final race of the Games.
Ancient Olympic events, by debut.Trumpeters' contest: Trumpeters and heralds competed in volume and endurance, and the winner earned the job of sounding the calls for the other events.

Famous numbers in psychology.Piaget's stages: Piaget's stages are sensorimotor, preoperational, concrete operational and formal operational, and he based them on watching his own children.
Famous numbers in psychology.Big Five traits: Openness, conscientiousness, extraversion, agreeableness and neuroticism form the most research-backed model of personality.
Famous numbers in psychology.Kohlberg's moral stages: Kohlberg's six stages fall into three levels, and he tested them with dilemmas like the Heinz dilemma, about stealing a drug for a dying wife.
Famous numbers in psychology.Miller's magic number: George Miller's 1956 paper said we hold about seven items, plus or minus two, in short-term memory; later estimates are lower, near four.
Famous numbers in psychology.Erikson's life stages: Each stage is a crisis, from trust versus mistrust in infancy to integrity versus despair in old age, spanning the whole life.
Famous numbers in psychology.Enneagram types: A popular personality system with little scientific support, with roots in twentieth-century spiritual teachings.
Famous numbers in psychology.Rorschach inkblot cards: Hermann Rorschach designed the ten inkblots in 1921; five are black and white, two black and red, and three colored.
Famous numbers in psychology.Myers-Briggs types: Mother and daughter Katharine Briggs and Isabel Myers built it from Carl Jung's ideas, and researchers question its reliability.
Famous numbers in psychology.Holmes-Rahe stress events: This stress scale gives each life event points; death of a spouse tops it at 100, and marriage scores 50.
Famous numbers in psychology.MMPI-2 questions: A famous personality and psychopathology questionnaire with 567 true-or-false items, taking an hour or more to finish.

Famous patients in medical history.Phineas Gage's iron rod: He survived an iron rod through his skull and frontal lobe, and reportedly his personality changed, though details were exaggerated.
Famous patients in medical history.Broca examines patient Tan: The patient could understand speech but only said tan, and his left frontal brain region is now called Broca's area.
Famous patients in medical history.Anna O's talking cure: Pseudonym of Bertha Pappenheim, who called her therapy chimney sweeping; she later pioneered social work in Germany.
Famous patients in medical history.Typhoid Mary identified: Mary Mallon, an Irish cook in New York, was a healthy carrier who infected dozens and spent about three decades in quarantine.
Famous patients in medical history.Henrietta Lacks's HeLa cells: Her cells were taken without consent and became the first immortal human cell line, helping to develop the polio vaccine.
Famous patients in medical history.Patient H.M.'s brain surgery: Henry Molaison lost the ability to form new memories after surgery for epilepsy, transforming memory science.
Famous patients in medical history.Bubble boy David Vetter born: Born with severe immune deficiency, he lived in a sterile plastic bubble for 12 years and died in 1984 after a transplant.
Famous patients in medical history.Karen Ann Quinlan's coma: Her parents' fight to remove her ventilator led to a right-to-die precedent, and she lived nearly a decade longer.
Famous patients in medical history.Ryan White diagnosed with AIDS: An Indiana teenager with hemophilia, infected through treatment, he was barred from school, and became the face of AIDS education.
Famous patients in medical history.Berlin patient cured of HIV: Timothy Ray Brown was cured through a stem-cell transplant from a donor with a CCR5 mutation that resists HIV.

Famous human feats, by how long they too.Bolt's 100 m record: Usain Bolt's 100 m record from the 2009 Berlin World Championships still stands, and he reached about 44 km/h.
Famous human feats, by how long they too.Bolt's 200 m record: Bolt's 200 m time is also from Berlin 2009, and no one has come close to it since.
Famous human feats, by how long they too.Bannister's mile: Roger Bannister's 1954 run in Oxford broke what many thought was a physical barrier, and it was beaten within two months.
Famous human feats, by how long they too.Gagarin's orbit of Earth: Yuri Gagarin's one orbit in Vostok 1 made him the first human in space, and the trip lasted 108 minutes.
Famous human feats, by how long they too.Kipchoge's sub-2 marathon: Eliud Kipchoge ran in Vienna with pacers and aided conditions, so it doesn't count as an official world record.
Famous human feats, by how long they too.Armstrong's Moonwalk: Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin spent around two and a half hours on the lunar surface during the first Moonwalk.
Famous human feats, by how long they too.Webb's Channel swim: Matthew Webb was the first person to swim the English Channel without aids, in 1875.
Famous human feats, by how long they too.Lindbergh's Atlantic flight: Charles Lindbergh's 1927 flight from New York to Paris lasted about 33 and a half hours.
Famous human feats, by how long they too.Apollo 11 mission: Apollo 11 took roughly eight days from launch to splashdown, and Armstrong's first words on the Moon were watched by about 600 million people.
Famous human feats, by how long they too.Amundsen's trek to the Pole: Roald Amundsen's team reached the South Pole in December 1911, using dogs and skis, beating Scott's party by about a month.

How much these drink containers hold.Espresso shot: An espresso shot is traditionally about 30 ml, and the word espresso means pressed out in Italian.
How much these drink containers hold.Shot glass: A US shot glass typically holds about 1.5 fluid ounces, though glasses vary quite a bit.
How much these drink containers hold.Glass of wine (pour): A glass of wine pour is about 150 ml, and a bottle holds around five glasses.
How much these drink containers hold.US soda can: The US soda can holds 355 ml, which is 12 fluid ounces, and a typical can is made of thin aluminum.
How much these drink containers hold.US pint glass: A US pint is smaller than an imperial pint, which is about 568 ml.
How much these drink containers hold.Wine bottle: A standard wine bottle holds 750 ml, which works out to about five average glasses.
How much these drink containers hold.7-Eleven Big Gulp: The Big Gulp was introduced by 7-Eleven in 1976, and larger sizes later followed.
How much these drink containers hold.Two-liter soda bottle: The 2-liter plastic soda bottle came along in the 1970s and was a big hit for its low cost.
How much these drink containers hold.Gallon jug of milk: A gallon of milk is about 3.8 liters, and it's the standard unit for milk in the US.
How much these drink containers hold.Half-barrel beer keg: A half-barrel keg is the standard keg in US bars, and it holds about 15.5 gallons and weighs over 160 pounds when full.

How long until the egg hatches?.House sparrow: A tiny songbird: its young hatch quickly and leave the nest in about two weeks.
How long until the egg hatches?.Rock pigeon: Both parents feed their chicks 'crop milk', a nutritious secretion, which is rare among birds.
How long until the egg hatches?.Chicken: Chicks peep inside the egg days before hatching and break out with a temporary egg tooth on the beak.
How long until the egg hatches?.Mallard: Ducklings can leave the nest within a day of hatching and swim almost immediately.
How long until the egg hatches?.Bald eagle: Their nests are the largest of any North American bird and can weigh over a tonne.
How long until the egg hatches?.Ostrich: The ostrich lays the largest egg of any living bird, equal to roughly two dozen chicken eggs.
How long until the egg hatches?.Emu: The male does the incubating alone, barely eating or drinking for weeks.
How long until the egg hatches?.Emperor penguin: The male balances a single egg on his feet through the Antarctic winter, without eating.
How long until the egg hatches?.Kiwi: A kiwi's egg can be about a fifth of the mother's weight, among the largest relative to body size of any bird.
How long until the egg hatches?.Tuatara: This New Zealand reptile is the last of an ancient lineage; its eggs can take over a year to hatch, and warmth decides the sex.

When these music charts and awards began.UK Singles Chart: The first number one was 'Here in My Heart' by Al Martino, in a chart compiled by NME.
When these music charts and awards began.Eurovision Song Contest: The first was held in Lugano, Switzerland, with seven countries; Swiss singer Lys Assia won.
When these music charts and awards began.Billboard Hot 100: Ricky Nelson's 'Poor Little Fool' became its first number one.
When these music charts and awards began.Grammy Awards: Domenico Modugno's 'Volare' won record of the year at the first ceremony.
When these music charts and awards began.Top of the Pops: The BBC show aired until 2006; the first episode was in Manchester and featured the Rolling Stones.
When these music charts and awards began.American Music Awards: Dick Clark started it after ABC lost the Grammys broadcast, and winners are chosen by fans.
When these music charts and awards began.Brit Awards: First held in 1977 to mark the Queen's Silver Jubilee; it became an annual event later.
When these music charts and awards began.MTV: The first video it aired was 'Video Killed the Radio Star' by The Buggles.
When these music charts and awards began.Rock Hall first inductions: Chuck Berry was among the first group of inductees, along with Elvis Presley.
When these music charts and awards began.Mercury Prize: Primal Scream's Screamadelica won first; judges pick the best album from the UK and Ireland.

Tech IPOs by year.Apple: Apple's 1980 float was the largest since Ford in 1956, and it instantly minted more millionaires than any company before it.
Tech IPOs by year.Microsoft: Microsoft went public at 21 dollars a share, and the stock's rise made co-founder Bill Gates a billionaire by age 31.
Tech IPOs by year.Netscape: Its browser launched a stock frenzy as it soared on its first day, helping to kick off the dot-com boom; AOL bought it later.
Tech IPOs by year.Amazon: Amazon went public as a mostly online bookseller at 18 dollars a share, and it did not turn a profit for years afterward.
Tech IPOs by year.Google: The search company chose an unusual auction-style offering, and its first shares sold for 85 dollars each.
Tech IPOs by year.Facebook: It was then the largest tech IPO ever, and its 104 billion dollar valuation came about eight years after it was launched in a dorm.
Tech IPOs by year.Twitter: It went public at 26 dollars a share and later became X, a name change that replaced the famous blue bird logo.
Tech IPOs by year.Snap: Its parent company's shares were sold without voting rights, a first for a big IPO, and the app popularised disappearing photos.
Tech IPOs by year.Airbnb: The home-rental platform went public during the pandemic, when travel had been hit hard, and its first-day price doubled.
Tech IPOs by year.Reddit: The social news site went public after years of cultivating its community, and many of its own users bought shares.

Airlines, by founding year.KLM: The Dutch carrier is the world's oldest airline still operating under its original name, and its name stands for Royal Dutch Airlines.
Airlines, by founding year.Qantas: The Australian airline's name stands for Queensland and Northern Territory Aerial Services, and it began by flying mail in the outback.
Airlines, by founding year.Aeroflot: The Soviet and now Russian airline's name means 'air fleet' and its winged hammer-and-sickle logo was famous.
Airlines, by founding year.Pan Am: The airline that pioneered international travel by flying boats put the 'jumbo jet' into service in 1970.
Airlines, by founding year.Air France: It was formed by merging several smaller French carriers, and it later merged with KLM to form Air France-KLM.
Airlines, by founding year.El Al: The Israeli airline is known for strict security, and in 1976 it was involved in the Entebbe hostage rescue.
Airlines, by founding year.Southwest Airlines: It is the origin of the low-fare model in the U.S., and its founder Herb Kelleher famously drank whiskey and smoked at work.
Airlines, by founding year.Ryanair: The Irish budget airline was built on the Southwest model, and it has become Europe's biggest by passengers.
Airlines, by founding year.easyJet: The orange-liveried airline began with two leased aircraft, and its founder Stelios Haji-Ioannou named it after himself.
Airlines, by founding year.JetBlue: The New York carrier offers free snacks and live TV at every seat, and it was launched with a focus on customer service.

The world's oldest universities, by foun.University of Bologna: Its founding date is often given as 1088, and it is regarded as the oldest university in continuous operation in the world.
The world's oldest universities, by foun.University of Oxford: Teaching began here in the late 11th century, and it grew rapidly after English students were forbidden from attending Paris.
The world's oldest universities, by foun.University of Paris: Also known as the Sorbonne, it grew out of the cathedral school of Notre-Dame, and it was where Thomas Aquinas taught.
The world's oldest universities, by foun.University of Cambridge: The university was founded by scholars who fled from Oxford after a dispute with townspeople, and it has produced over 100 Nobel laureates.
The world's oldest universities, by foun.University of Salamanca: The Spanish university, founded by King Alfonso IX, is where Columbus is said to have defended his plan to sail west.
The world's oldest universities, by foun.Harvard: The oldest institution of higher education in the U.S. was named after a minister who left it his library, and it is in Massachusetts.
The world's oldest universities, by foun.Yale: It was founded in Connecticut as the Collegiate School, and was later named after Elihu Yale, a merchant who gave it books.
The world's oldest universities, by foun.Princeton: It began as the College of New Jersey, and it moved to its present town in 1756, and Einstein worked at its Institute for Advanced Study.
The world's oldest universities, by foun.MIT: The Massachusetts Institute of Technology was started with a focus on practical science, and it moved to its Cambridge campus in 1916.
The world's oldest universities, by foun.Stanford: It was founded by a railroad baron in memory of his son, and it later became the heart of Silicon Valley.

Nature's speeds, from glacial to lightni.Stalactite growth: Dripping water leaves a thin film of calcite, so one a metre long can take about ten thousand years.
Nature's speeds, from glacial to lightni.Continental drift: About as fast as fingernails grow, which is how fast the Atlantic Ocean widens.
Nature's speeds, from glacial to lightni.Typical glacier flow: Jakobshavn Isbræ in Greenland has been clocked at more than 40 m a day, far above a typical glacier.
Nature's speeds, from glacial to lightni.Pāhoehoe lava flow: This smooth, ropy Hawaiian lava gets its name from the Hawaiian language.
Nature's speeds, from glacial to lightni.Falling raindrop: Despite the cartoon teardrop shape, raindrops are round or flattened like little hamburger buns.
Nature's speeds, from glacial to lightni.Record wind gust (1996): It struck Barrow Island, Australia, during Cyclone Olivia, and is the highest surface gust ever officially measured.
Nature's speeds, from glacial to lightni.Tsunami in open ocean: In deep ocean it moves at jet speed yet is barely noticeable, growing tall only near shore.
Nature's speeds, from glacial to lightni.Sound in air: Chuck Yeager first flew faster than this in 1947, and it is the speed called Mach 1.
Nature's speeds, from glacial to lightni.Earthquake P-wave: These 'primary' waves arrive first, which is how earthquake early-warning systems get seconds to alert people.
Nature's speeds, from glacial to lightni.Lightning return stroke: The flash you see travels at roughly a third of the speed of light, about 100,000 km a second.

When these famous scientists were born.Archimedes: The Greek mathematician from Syracuse is said to have shouted 'Eureka!' on spotting how to measure a crown's volume in his bath.
When these famous scientists were born.Nicolaus Copernicus: He proposed that Earth orbits the Sun, and he held off publishing until the year of his death in 1543.
When these famous scientists were born.Galileo Galilei: He pointed a telescope at the sky and saw Jupiter's four big moons, and he was later put under house arrest for his views.
When these famous scientists were born.Isaac Newton: He formulated the laws of motion and gravity, and also invented calculus; he later ran the Royal Mint.
When these famous scientists were born.Charles Darwin: He sailed on HMS Beagle as a young man, and his Galapagos finches helped inspire the theory of evolution by natural selection.
When these famous scientists were born.Louis Pasteur: He saved lives with the first rabies vaccine, and his heating process, pasteurization, is named for him.
When these famous scientists were born.Nikola Tesla: The Serbian-American engineer developed alternating current systems, and the unit of magnetic flux density is named for him.
When these famous scientists were born.Marie Curie: The first woman to win a Nobel Prize and the only one to win in two sciences, physics and chemistry.
When these famous scientists were born.Albert Einstein: His 1905 'miracle year' produced four world-changing papers, and he won the Nobel for the photoelectric effect, not relativity.
When these famous scientists were born.Stephen Hawking: He wrote A Brief History of Time while living with ALS for decades, and spoke through a speech-generating device.

Density: from thin gas to a neutron star.Interstellar gas: Space isn't truly empty, but the gas between the stars averages around one atom per cubic centimetre or less.
Density: from thin gas to a neutron star.Air at sea level: A cubic metre of air at sea level has a mass of about 1.2 kg, and all of it adds up to the pressure on you.
Density: from thin gas to a neutron star.Saturn: Saturn would float in a big enough bathtub, because its average density is lower than water's.
Density: from thin gas to a neutron star.Water: Water is unusual because ice is less dense than liquid, so lakes freeze from the top down.
Density: from thin gas to a neutron star.The Sun (average): Although mostly hydrogen, the Sun averages about 40 percent denser than water, thanks to its enormous gravity.
Density: from thin gas to a neutron star.Earth: Earth is the densest planet in the solar system, thanks to its iron-nickel core.
Density: from thin gas to a neutron star.Gold: A gold cube 10 cm on a side would weigh about 19 kg, which is why gold nuggets settle in stream beds.
Density: from thin gas to a neutron star.The Sun's core: The core is far denser than gold yet stays a gas-like plasma because of its heat, about 15 million degrees Celsius.
Density: from thin gas to a neutron star.White dwarf: A teaspoon of white dwarf would weigh several tonnes; our Sun will end its life as one.
Density: from thin gas to a neutron star.Neutron star: A teaspoon of neutron star would weigh billions of tonnes, packing the mass of a sun into a city-sized ball.

Milestones in grocery shopping.Kroger founded: Barney Kroger opened his first shop in Cincinnati, and the chain grew into one of the largest grocers in the United States.
Milestones in grocery shopping.Piggly Wiggly self-service: Clarence Saunders' Memphis store was the first to let customers pick products off shelves themselves instead of asking a clerk.
Milestones in grocery shopping.Tesco founded: Founded by Jack Cohen from a London market stall, the name blends his surname with the initials of a tea supplier, T. E. Stockwell.
Milestones in grocery shopping.Shopping cart invented: Oklahoma grocer Sylvan Goldman invented it, a folding chair on wheels, and at first shoppers refused to use it.
Milestones in grocery shopping.Trader Joe's opens: Joe Coulombe opened his first one in Pasadena, California, and gave it a nautical, island-trader theme.
Milestones in grocery shopping.First barcode scanned (gum): A pack of Wrigley's gum became the first item scanned, at a supermarket in Troy, Ohio; barcodes were a slow start but went global.
Milestones in grocery shopping.Whole Foods opens: It started in Austin, Texas, with a small natural foods store staffed by only a handful of employees, before it grew into a national chain.
Milestones in grocery shopping.Costco opens: The first warehouse opened in Seattle, and its hot dog and soda combo has held a famously low price for decades.
Milestones in grocery shopping.Instacart founded: The delivery app started in San Francisco, and its shoppers pick groceries from local stores for customers to receive in hours.
Milestones in grocery shopping.Amazon Go opens to public: Shoppers just walk out and cameras and sensors work out what they took, billing their account without any checkout line.

Animal numbers trivia.Humps on a dromedary: Dromedaries have one, and Bactrian camels have two; the hump stores fat, not water.
Animal numbers trivia.Chambers in a fish's heart: A fish's heart has just two chambers, an atrium and a ventricle, while humans have four.
Animal numbers trivia.Stomach chambers in a cow: Grazing animals like cows chew cud, and the four compartments let microbes break down grass in the first one, the rumen.
Animal numbers trivia.Toes on a cat's front paw: Cats have five toes on each front paw but four on the back, and some cats are born with extra toes.
Animal numbers trivia.Neck bones in a giraffe: A giraffe has the same number of neck bones as a human or a mouse, only much longer.
Animal numbers trivia.Arms on an octopus: An octopus has about two thirds of its neurons in its arms, so each arm can act almost on its own.
Animal numbers trivia.Legs on a lobster: The name decapod means ten-footed, a group that includes lobsters, crabs and shrimp.
Animal numbers trivia.Teeth in a dog: An adult dog has about 42 permanent teeth, compared with 32 for most adult humans.
Animal numbers trivia.Bones in an adult human: Babies are born with about 300 bones that fuse together over time into the adult count.
Animal numbers trivia.Muscles in an elephant's trunk: An elephant's trunk has no bones, and its estimated 40,000 muscle units let it pick up a single peanut or a tree trunk.

Black-and-white animals by weight.Black-and-white warbler: Unlike most warblers, it creeps along tree trunks and branches like a nuthatch, probing bark for insects.
Black-and-white animals by weight.Magpie: It is one of the few animals to pass the mirror test, recognizing itself in a reflection.
Black-and-white animals by weight.Atlantic puffin: Its beak can hold several small fish at once, thanks to backward-pointing spines on the tongue and palate.
Black-and-white animals by weight.Striped skunk: It can spray a smelly liquid accurately up to around 3 m, and its bold stripes warn predators in advance.
Black-and-white animals by weight.European badger: Its setts, tunnel systems that may be centuries old, are dug and extended by generations of badgers.
Black-and-white animals by weight.Emperor penguin: Males balance the single egg on their feet through the Antarctic winter, going about two months without eating.
Black-and-white animals by weight.Giant panda: Most of its day goes on eating bamboo, and its "thumb" is really an extended wrist bone.
Black-and-white animals by weight.Plains zebra: No two zebras have the same stripe pattern, which may help deter biting flies.
Black-and-white animals by weight.Holstein cow: This dairy breed is the world's top milk producer, and a good cow gives dozens of liters a day.
Black-and-white animals by weight.Orca: Despite the name "killer whale", it is the largest dolphin, hunting in family pods with traditions of their own.

Books of the Book of Mormon, in order.Jacob: Jacob is the third book of the Book of Mormon and is named for the younger brother of Nephi, who was a priest and teacher.
Books of the Book of Mormon, in order.Enos: Enos is a short book about a man's prayer in the wilderness, and it is among the book's smallest.
Books of the Book of Mormon, in order.Jarom: Jarom is one of the shortest books, with only 15 verses, telling of a lineage of Nephite record-keepers.
Books of the Book of Mormon, in order.Omni: Omni is a short book with several authors passing the records along, and it introduces the people of Zarahemla.
Books of the Book of Mormon, in order.Mosiah: Mosiah describes the reign of King Benjamin and a king's decision to establish rule by judges.
Books of the Book of Mormon, in order.Alma: Alma is the longest book in the Book of Mormon, and it contains the story of Alma the Younger's conversion.
Books of the Book of Mormon, in order.Helaman: Helaman recounts Nephite and Lamanite conflict, with the prophet Nephi, and a Gadianton robber threat.
Books of the Book of Mormon, in order.Mormon: Mormon's book records the final decline of the Nephite civilization, edited by the man the Book of Mormon was named for.
Books of the Book of Mormon, in order.Ether: Ether tells the story of the Jaredites, a people who sailed across the sea in barges to the promised land.
Books of the Book of Mormon, in order.Moroni: Moroni is the final book, and Moroni, an ancient prophet, is the angel shown on many LDS temples.

Number of countries bordering each.Haiti: Haiti shares the island of Hispaniola with the Dominican Republic, and the border between them is a significant cultural and economic divide.
Number of countries bordering each.Bhutan: Bhutan is landlocked between China and India, and it measures national success by Gross National Happiness.
Number of countries bordering each.Vietnam: Vietnam borders China, Laos and Cambodia, and its long S-shaped coast faces the South China Sea.
Number of countries bordering each.Belgium: Belgium borders France, Germany, Luxembourg and the Netherlands, and the town of Baarle-Hertog has Dutch enclaves within it.
Number of countries bordering each.Switzerland: Switzerland is bordered by France, Germany, Austria, Liechtenstein and Italy, and it has four national languages.
Number of countries bordering each.Afghanistan: Afghanistan lies at a crossroads of Central and South Asia, and the Wakhan Corridor links it to China.
Number of countries bordering each.Saudi Arabia: Saudi Arabia borders Jordan, Iraq, Kuwait, Qatar, UAE, Oman and Yemen, plus a causeway to Bahrain, and has no permanent rivers.
Number of countries bordering each.Tanzania: Tanzania borders eight countries, including Kenya and Uganda, and is home to Mount Kilimanjaro and the Serengeti.
Number of countries bordering each.DR Congo: The Democratic Republic of the Congo is the second-largest African country, and borders nine countries, and the Congo River runs through it.
Number of countries bordering each.Russia: Russia borders 14 countries, from Norway to North Korea, which is more than any other country except China, which also has 14.

First flights of famous aircraft.Wright Flyer: Orville's first flight on 17 December 1903 lasted 12 seconds and covered about 120 feet.
First flights of famous aircraft.Sopwith Camel: The WWI fighter, named for the hump over its guns, shot down more enemy aircraft than any other Allied fighter.
First flights of famous aircraft.Spirit of St. Louis: Lindbergh flew solo across the Atlantic in 33 hours, and had no forward window because a fuel tank was in the way.
First flights of famous aircraft.Douglas DC-3: It made passenger flying profitable in the 1930s, and some are still flying today.
First flights of famous aircraft.Messerschmitt Me 262 (jet): This was the first operational jet fighter, but it came too late to change the war.
First flights of famous aircraft.Boeing 707: This brought the jet age to ordinary passengers, and cut Atlantic crossings to a few hours.
First flights of famous aircraft.SR-71 Blackbird: It cruised above Mach 3 and outran missiles, once flying coast to coast across the US in about 67 minutes.
First flights of famous aircraft.Boeing 747: The Jumbo Jet's hump holds the cockpit upstairs, and it was the world's largest passenger plane for decades until the A380.
First flights of famous aircraft.Airbus A380: It can seat more than 800 people and is the largest passenger airliner ever built.
First flights of famous aircraft.Boeing 787 Dreamliner: The Dreamliner is largely carbon-fibre, with bigger windows and lower cabin altitude for passenger comfort.

Distance from London (as the crow flies).Paris: The Eurostar takes about two hours and sixteen minutes through the Channel Tunnel.
Distance from London (as the crow flies).Dublin: It is one of the busiest international air routes in Europe, despite the short flight.
Distance from London (as the crow flies).Berlin: Its roughly 1,700 bridges are said to outnumber those of Venice.
Distance from London (as the crow flies).Rome: Traditionally founded in 753 BC, it's known as the Eternal City.
Distance from London (as the crow flies).Moscow: Russia's capital is the largest city entirely within Europe.
Distance from London (as the crow flies).Cairo: The city is home to the Great Pyramid, the last surviving wonder of the ancient world.
Distance from London (as the crow flies).New York: It's five hours behind London for most of the year, so a morning call here is lunchtime across the Atlantic.
Distance from London (as the crow flies).Mumbai: It was called Bombay until 1995, when it took its older name from the goddess Mumbadevi.
Distance from London (as the crow flies).Tokyo: Its metropolitan area is the most populated in the world, with roughly 37 million people.
Distance from London (as the crow flies).Sydney: Its Opera House was designed by Jørn Utzon, who left the project and never saw it finished.

Tempo markings by speed.Larghissimo: Italian for very, very broad: the slowest marking, so rare that most players will never meet it on a page of music.
Tempo markings by speed.Grave: Italian for serious or solemn, it opens Beethoven's Pathetique Sonata with heavy, dramatic chords.
Tempo markings by speed.Largo: Italian for broad; Handel's Ombra mai fu, a famous slow piece, is often called simply Handel's Largo.
Tempo markings by speed.Adagio: Italian for at ease; Barber's Adagio for Strings is perhaps the most famous slow piece in the repertoire.
Tempo markings by speed.Andante: Italian for walking, so a leisurely walking pace, and the middle tempo of the classical scale.
Tempo markings by speed.Moderato: Meaning moderate, its numbers were attached only after Maelzel's metronome came into use in the 1810s.
Tempo markings by speed.Allegro: Meaning cheerful in Italian, it began as a mood more than a speed, and later settled into the fast tempo we know.
Tempo markings by speed.Vivace: Italian for lively, it sits between Allegro and Presto and is found in the dancing finales of many symphonies.
Tempo markings by speed.Presto: Italian for quick; the finale of Beethoven's Moonlight Sonata is marked Presto agitato and is notoriously fiendish.
Tempo markings by speed.Prestissimo: The fastest standard marking, meaning as quickly as possible, and it demands real virtuosity from players.

When these creatures first appeared.Jellyfish: Fossils show them in ancient seas, though they have no brain, heart or bones, so they are among the oldest animals.
When these creatures first appeared.Horseshoe crabs: Despite the name, they're closer kin to spiders than crabs, and their blue blood is used to test vaccines for contamination.
When these creatures first appeared.Cockroach ancestors: The 'roachoids' scuttled around in coal-swamp forests before dinosaurs even existed.
When these creatures first appeared.Dinosaurs: The first ones appeared in the Triassic, and birds, their living descendants, still share the planet with us.
When these creatures first appeared.Ants: They descend from wasp-like ancestors and today live on every continent except Antarctica.
When these creatures first appeared.Bees: They evolved from predatory wasps that switched to eating pollen as flowering plants spread.
When these creatures first appeared.Primates: Early members were tiny tree-dwelling creatures, and your lineage began among them.
When these creatures first appeared.Cats: The earliest relatives were small forest dwellers like Proailurus, which looked something like a civet.
When these creatures first appeared.Mammoths: Some lived on Wrangel Island until about 4,000 years ago, long after the Egyptian pyramids were built.
When these creatures first appeared.Homo sapiens: The oldest known fossils come from Jebel Irhoud in Morocco, much older than once thought.

Foods named after places, by latitude.Hamburger: Named for Hamburg, Germany, though the ground-beef sandwich we know was popularised in the United States.
Foods named after places, by latitude.Edam cheese: Named for a Dutch town. Its red wax coating protected cheese on long sea voyages.
Foods named after places, by latitude.Cheddar cheese: Named for a gorge in Somerset, where the cheese was traditionally matured in caves.
Foods named after places, by latitude.Frankfurter: Named for Frankfurt am Main. Americans shortened it to 'frank', then applied the hot-dog nickname.
Foods named after places, by latitude.Champagne (Reims): Only sparkling wine from this French region may legally carry the name.
Foods named after places, by latitude.Dijon mustard: Though named for Dijon, the name is not legally protected, so the mustard can be made anywhere.
Foods named after places, by latitude.Parmesan: The real Parmigiano Reggiano comes from near Parma and is aged at least a year, stamped on the rind.
Foods named after places, by latitude.Buffalo wings: Invented at the Anchor Bar in Buffalo, New York, around 1964. No buffalo was involved.
Foods named after places, by latitude.Neapolitan pizza: UNESCO recognised the art of the Neapolitan pizza maker. Margherita is said to honour Queen Margherita.
Foods named after places, by latitude.Cayenne pepper: Named for the city of Cayenne in French Guiana, and the only item here near the equator.

When these sneakers first laced up.Converse All Star: Named after Chuck Taylor, a basketball player who promoted the shoe from the 1920s.
When these sneakers first laced up.Puma Suede: Debuted in 1968. Sprinter Tommie Smith held up Pumas on the podium at the Mexico City Olympics.
When these sneakers first laced up.Adidas Superstar: Its rubber shell toe made it a basketball favourite, then Run-DMC's 1986 'My Adidas' made it a hip-hop icon.
When these sneakers first laced up.Nike Cortez: Designed by Nike co-founder Bill Bowerman. Forrest Gump wore a pair when running across America.
When these sneakers first laced up.Vans Old Skool: The first Vans with the 'jazz stripe', a side line that began as founder Paul Van Doren's doodle.
When these sneakers first laced up.Nike Air Force 1: Named after the US presidential plane, it was the first basketball shoe with an Air cushioning unit.
When these sneakers first laced up.Air Jordan 1: The NBA banned the black-and-red colours in 1985, reportedly fining Michael Jordan $5,000 a game.
When these sneakers first laced up.Nike Air Max 1: Tinker Hatfield's visible air window was inspired by the exposed pipes of Paris's Pompidou Centre.
When these sneakers first laced up.Reebok Pump: Its built-in pump inflated the shoe. Dee Brown pumped them up before his 1991 dunk contest win.
When these sneakers first laced up.Adidas Yeezy Boost: Boost foam comes from the chemical company BASF. Adidas ended its Kanye West deal in 2022.

An apple's year, step by step.Buds swell in spring: Apple trees need a winter chill, hundreds of hours of cold, before their buds wake properly in spring.
An apple's year, step by step.Blossom opens: Apple blossoms open pink and fade to white, and a tree may bloom with thousands of flowers yet keep only a fraction as fruit.
An apple's year, step by step.Bees carry pollen: Most apple varieties can't pollinate themselves, so orchards plant compatible varieties together and often bring in hives of honeybees.
An apple's year, step by step.Petals drop: Once the petals fall, the flower's base begins swelling into fruit, and trees shed surplus tiny fruitlets in what growers call the June drop.
An apple's year, step by step.Tiny green apple forms: Apples belong to the rose family, making them cousins of pears, plums, almonds and roses themselves.
An apple's year, step by step.Apple swells over summer: About a quarter of an apple's volume is air, which is why it floats in water.
An apple's year, step by step.Skin blushes red: The red comes from anthocyanin pigments, boosted by sunlight and cool autumn nights, so apples shaded by leaves stay paler.
An apple's year, step by step.Picked in autumn: Over 7,000 apple varieties exist worldwide, yet most supermarkets stock only a handful of them.
An apple's year, step by step.Sold at a market: Apples can be stored for months in cold rooms with carefully controlled air, which is how fresh-tasting ones reach shops in spring.
An apple's year, step by step.Crunched in a lunchbox: A crisp apple crunches because its cells snap open and spray juice, while a mealy one just goes soft.

Apollo missions to the Moon, by launch.First crew to orbit the Moon: Apollo 8 astronauts read from Genesis on Christmas Eve and took the famous Earthrise photograph.
Apollo missions to the Moon, by launch.Lunar module test in orbit: Apollo 9 tested the lunar module in Earth orbit, with the crew calling it Spider.
Apollo missions to the Moon, by launch.Dress rehearsal near the Moon: Apollo 10 flew within about 15 kilometres of the surface, with its modules named Snoopy and Charlie Brown.
Apollo missions to the Moon, by launch.First footsteps: Armstrong and Aldrin spent about two and a half hours outside while Collins orbited alone.
Apollo missions to the Moon, by launch.Pinpoint landing near Surveyor: Apollo 12 landed near Surveyor 3 and brought back parts of the probe's camera.
Apollo missions to the Moon, by launch.Oxygen tank explosion: The crew said Houston, we've had a problem, and used the lunar module as a lifeboat to return safely.
Apollo missions to the Moon, by launch.Shepard hits golf balls: Alan Shepard, the first American in space, hit golf balls with a makeshift club.
Apollo missions to the Moon, by launch.First lunar rover: Apollo 15 brought the rover, letting astronauts travel kilometres from the lander.
Apollo missions to the Moon, by launch.Landing at Descartes: Apollo 16 landed in the highlands, and John Young later flew the space shuttle.
Apollo missions to the Moon, by launch.Last humans on the Moon: Gene Cernan was the last person to walk on the Moon, alongside Harrison Schmitt, the only geologist to do so.
